root_cause.text: In EROFS file-backed mounts, `erofs_fileio_ki_complete()` treated a short positive return from `vfs_iocb_iter_read()` as successful completion and finalized the whole bio, so folios that were not actually filled due to an interrupt-driven short read were incorrectly marked uptodate.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that `vfs_iocb_iter_read()` can be interrupted by `SIGKILL`, “returning the number of bytes actually copied,” after which “unused folios in bio are unexpectedly marked as uptodate”; the patch removes the short-read handling that did `bio_advance(...); zero_fill_bio(...)` and instead changes `ret` to `-EIO` when `ret >= 0 && ret != rq->bio.bi_iter.bi_size`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In EROFS file-backed mounts, `erofs_fileio_ki_complete()` treated a short positive return from `vfs_iocb_iter_read()` as successful completion and finalized the whole bio, so folios that were not actually filled due to an interrupt-driven short read were incorrectly marked uptodate.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states that `vfs_iocb_iter_read()` can be interrupted by `SIGKILL`, “returning the number of bytes actually copied,” after which “unused folios in bio are unexpectedly marked as uptodate”; the patch removes the short-read handling that did `bio_advance(...); zero_fill_bio(...)` and instead changes `ret` to `-EIO` when `ret >= 0 && ret != rq->bio.bi_iter.bi_size`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Treat short successful file I/O completions as -EIO instead of zero-filling the remaining bio data.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a conditional block in erofs_fileio_ki_complete() that previously advanced the bio by the returned byte count and zero-filled the remaining bio on a short nonnegative completion, with a single statement that instead sets ret to -EIO when ret is nonnegative but smaller than rq->bio.bi_iter.bi_size.
intent_record.how: At runtime, partial successful completions are no longer treated as recoverable by padding the unread portion with zeros; they are now converted into an I/O error, causing the request to be handled as a failure instead of silently completing with zero-filled data.

grouping_result.intent: Treat short successful file I/O completions as -EIO instead of zero-filling the remaining bio data.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the root cause: short positive reads from file-backed I/O were being treated as successful completion. Converting short successful completions to -EIO prevents incorrectly finalizing the full bio and marking incompletely filled folios uptodate.

candidates.rationale: This condition treats any non-negative short read as a normal completion path instead of an error, which is the core root cause described.
Zero-filling the remainder after a short positive read masks the incomplete I/O and allows the bio to be finalized as if all folios were correctly populated.
Advancing the bio by the short-read length is part of incorrectly converting a partial completion into an apparently completed bio.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition is the key logic error: it classifies a short positive return from the backing file read as a handled completion path rather than a failure, enabling the bio to be completed even though not all requested data was actually read.
This statement masks the short read by zero-filling unread portions, which causes the bio to look fully satisfied and lets folios be marked uptodate despite incomplete backing-file I/O.
This advances the bio after only a partial positive read, contributing to the incorrect treatment of the request as successfully completed instead of surfacing the short read as an error.

I/O requests beyond the end of the filesystem should be
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit bc804a8d7e865ef47fb7edcaf5e77d18bf444ebc
Author: Gao Xiang <xiang@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Jan 30 15:54:22 2026 +0800

    erofs: handle end of filesystem properly for file-backed mounts
    
    I/O requests beyond the end of the filesystem should be zeroed out,
    similar to loopback devices and that is what we expect.
    
    Fixes: ce63cb62d794 ("erofs: support unencoded inodes for fileio")
    Signed-off-by: Gao Xiang <hsiangkao@linux.alibaba.com>

diff --git a/fs/erofs/fileio.c b/f
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because it contains the completion logic identified in the root cause. In this commit, the old vulnerable construct `if (ret > 0) { ... ret = 0; }` is no longer present. Instead, the code does `if (ret >= 0 && ret != rq->bio.bi_iter.bi_size) { bio_advance(&rq->bio, ret); zero_fill_bio(&rq->bio); }`, and later calls `erofs_onlinefolio_end(fi.folio, ret < 0, false);`. This means a short positive read is no longer blindly converted into full success by forcing `ret = 0`; the unread tail is explicitly zero-filled before folios are completed. However, the specific fix for the stated root cause is not fully present here: for a short positive return caused by an interrupt-driven partial read, this code still treats the operation as successful for folio completion (`ret < 0` is false), merely zero-filling the remainder. The root cause describes that short positive returns from `vfs_iocb_iter_read()` should not be finalized as successful completion of the whole bio when data was not actually read. Therefore the original vulnerable construct is absent (`has_bug=false`), but the code does not yet contain the later correct handling for interrupted short reads (`is_fixed=false`).
